result.summary: This narrow residential street provides a continuous pedestrian environment with sidewalks on both sides and buildings fronting directly onto the walkway. The constrained roadway width likely maintains low vehicle speeds, though the lack of a buffer and the presence of garage entrances create potential conflict points.

hazards.name: Garage/Driveway Conflict
hazards.description: A garage door opens directly onto the sidewalk, creating a risk of collision between exiting vehicles and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, dark grey garage door.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is immediately adjacent to the roadway with no physical separation or furniture zone, increasing exposure to moving traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street along the entire block.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Implement a raised crosswalk at the upcoming intersection to slow traffic and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and prevent vehicles from parking too close to the corner.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a paved walkway flush with a narrow residential street, serving as access for multiple private garages. This configuration creates a shared-space dynamic without clear delineation or physical protection for pedestrians from vehicle movements. While the low-traffic residential setting and mature trees are beneficial, the frequent driveway conflicts and lack of curbs reduce overall safety.

hazards.name: Frequent driveway crossings
hazards.description: Multiple ground-floor garages create frequent conflict points where vehicles must cross the pedestrian walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Ground floor of the brick building

hazards.name: Lack of vertical separation
hazards.description: The absence of a raised curb allows vehicles to easily encroach upon the pedestrian space.
hazards.location_in_image: Transition between the asphalt roadway and concrete walkway

interventions.title: Delineate Pedestrian Zone
interventions.description: Use contrasting pavement materials, colors, or textures to clearly distinguish the pedestrian path from vehicle access areas.

interventions.title: Install Protective Bollards
interventions.description: Place bollards along the edge of the walkway to prevent vehicle encroachment while maintaining access to private garages.

result.summary: This is a narrow, tree-lined residential street with continuous sidewalks on both sides. The narrow roadway and presence of parked cars likely encourage low vehicle speeds, though the lack of marked crossings and potential sightline obstructions from parked vehicles are notable.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the left side of the street may block the view of pedestrians attempting to cross the road, especially children.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street where cars are parked

hazards.name: Narrow effective sidewalk width
hazards.description: Large trees planted within the sidewalk area reduce the clear walking width for pedestrians, particularly those with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street where mature trees are located

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the ends of the block or mid-block to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: If there is significant pedestrian demand, a marked crosswalk with appropriate signage would improve safety and visibility.

result.summary: The image shows a residential sidewalk environment where buildings directly abut the walkway. A mature tree and several potted plants create minor physical obstructions, and the concrete pavement exhibits some cracking and unevenness.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A mature tree is located in the center of the paved walkway, significantly narrowing the clear path for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Uneven Pavement
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven concrete slabs on the sidewalk create potential tripping hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Lower left and center sidewalk area

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair
interventions.description: Level and repair cracked concrete slabs to provide a smooth, accessible surface for all users.

interventions.title: Clear Path Maintenance
interventions.description: Ensure that private encroachments like potted plants do not further restrict the pedestrian clear zone.
